To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the cesium-rich Cs1 − x(NH4xHSO4 ( x = 0.22) shows two successive superproton phase transitions at 380 and 407 K in cooling process and (2) each of the ammoniun-rich Cs1 - x(NH4)xHSO4 compounds ( x = 0,54 and 0,82) shows a single superproton phase transition.
the superprotonic transitions are associated with the reorientation of the NH4+ dipole in Cs1 −x(NH4) xHSO4.
the superprotonic transition in the ammonium–cesium mixed hydrogen sulfate Cs1 − x (NH4)xHSO 4 is related to the reorientation of the dipolar NH4 group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of superprotonic conductivity in Cs1 −x(NH4) xHSO4 solid electrolyte.
the superprotonic properties of Cs1 − xNH4xHSO4.
the study of the phase transitions of the superprotonic conductor CsHSO4 and its solid solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the superprotonic transitions in Cs1 −x(NH4) x HSO4 are caused by the reorientational motion of the NH4+ dipole group.
there are two types of superprotonic phases in the Cs1 − x (NH4)xHSO system, i.e., the one originated from the CsHSOs lattice and the other from the ammonium-rich lattice.
the superprotonic transitions in Cs1 − x(NH4) xHSO4 are closely related to the reorientational motion of NH4+ ion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the superprotonic transitions in Cs1 −x(NH4x)HSO4 can be classified into three types depending on the x value.
a superprotonic transition in the cesium ammonium sulfate system can be induced by the reorientational motion of NH4+ ions.
the protonic conduction mechanism in the superprotonic Cs1 −x(NH4) x HSO4 is closely related to the reorientational dynamics of NH4+ ion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase transition temperature of Cs1 −x(NH4x)HSO4 can be easily tuned by the ammonium concentration.
the superprotonic transitions can be induced in the cesium ammonium hydrogen sulfate (NH4CsHSO4) system by the substitution of Cs+ with NH4+ in the crystal structure.
the superprotonic transition temperature of Cs1 −x(NH4xHSO4 can be tuned by changing the Cs+/NH4+ ratio.
